_source: docs/eras/luv.md, '3. HTS magnet works' (package LuV-A4) and decision 13 (the HTS coil's 144 mB of trinium). Real: the CFS and MIT SPARC toroidal field model coil (20 T, 2021), SMES (BPA's 30 MJ unit, 1980s), vacuum-pressure impregnation and cold testing in magnet manufacturing.
_how_it_is_used: Read by startup_scripts/grindless/luv/hts_magnet_works.js (the charge, shown on the controller) and server_scripts/grindless/luv/hts_magnet_works.js (one gtceu:magnet_winding recipe per entry, id grindless:magnet_winding/<name>, with the data key grindless_magnet_winding = <name> for its EMI line); by the smoke test tools/test/overlay/kubejs/server_scripts/gg_test_luv_a4.js. Nothing here is repeated in code.

charge: the cold-test charge every entry with "charge": true carries, as GTM's non-consumed fluid input (notConsumableFluid, chance 0): needed in an input hatch to start, never drained, taken once whatever the overclock or the parallel hatch's copies.

recipes[]: name (the recipe's id and lang key), circuit (the programmed circuit that picks it: every entry has its own, so GTM's lookup keeps one recipe per path), itemsIn / fluidsIn (consumed), itemsOut, eut and duration (GTM's EU/t and ticks; marked (tune) in the design until the integrated bench run). The SMES cell's output is the LuV row's cell of tables/wireless_energy.json (its cellMadeBy names this machine); a Node test keeps the two tables in step.

recipes.name: hts_coil
recipes._why: GTM's own ladder: gtceu:assembler/superconducting_coil_luv takes 3,456 mB of trinium and 32 ITBTC double wires. Wound tape takes a twenty-fourth: one Mk1's 43 coils in under an hour of one x4 naquadah plant (decision 13, tune).

recipes.name: luv_smes_cell
recipes._why: The wireless network's LuV cell: superconducting magnetic energy storage, 983,040,000 EU (tables/wireless_energy.json, six LuV vanadium batteries).

recipes.name: coilgun_coil_casing
recipes._why: The coilgun probe launcher's coils (Ganymede): Hg-1223, HV's superconductor, wound and potted.

recipes.name: magnetic_bearing
recipes._why: Tetrataenite (L1_0 FeNi, the belt's meteoric magnet, rare-earth free) rods on an HSS-S ring: the rotating hydroponic ring's bearings.

recipes.name: seeded_gdbco_growth
recipes._why: UIV-A8, line 23: top-seeded melt growth of bulk GdBCO: a neodymium-based seed crystal on the Gd-123 melt in the cold-test helium, grown over hours (Cardwell and Durrell's single-domain bulks).

recipes.name: strand_stator
recipes._why: UXV-A8 (docs/eras/uxv.md, lines 34 and 35): pasta strand wire wound round a tetrataenite lamination stack, potted in epoxy and cold-tested in the helium charge: the UXV motor's stator.

recipes.name: rebco_pancake
recipes._why: OpV-A1 (docs/eras/opv.md line 8): REBCO coated conductor wound into a no-insulation double pancake (the SPARC TFMC's winding) with chain strand wire terminals, the epoxy as the turn-to-turn bond.

recipes.name: rebco_training
recipes._why: OpV-A1 (docs/eras/opv.md line 8): the potted pancake ramped in the cold-test helium through its training quenches until it holds full current.

recipes.name: octupole_winding
recipes._why: OpV-B3a line 27: slit REBCO tape wound into the octupole's racetrack coils over niobium-titanium foil shims, wetted in epoxy (the CVI furnace potts it next).

recipes.name: octupole_trap_magnet
recipes._why: OpV-B3a line 27: the potted and helium-cooled winding is quench-trained in the cold-test helium inside a tungsten steel former: the F1 octupole_trap_magnet.

recipes.name: max_coil_winding
recipes._why: MAX-A2 line L9 (c11): stabilised REBCO tape wound onto the CMC coil former with horizon strand wire and potted in epoxy, ramped in the cold-test helium.

recipes.name: pinned_rebco_web
recipes._why: MAX-B1 line L2 (c12): the REBCO-on-PBO web ramped in the cold-test helium while a lattice of flux-pinning columns is grown through it, potted in epoxy.

recipes.name: smes_toroid_winding
recipes._why: MAX-W (docs/eras/max.md, L27 step 3): eight turns of thick REBCO tape wound round a chain strand former and potted in epoxy, ramped in the cold-test helium.

recipes.name: fcl_coil
recipes._why: MAX-A4 line L39 (c14): eight turns of thick-film limiter tape wound with horizon strand wire and potted in epoxy, ramped in the cold-test helium.
